entries.clue: Queen has a good rage over misguided leader in a pickle (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue the rage sits on top of what follows, closing the answer
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Qu. is a standard abbreviation of queen

annotation.surface: A furious queen rages at a bungling prime minister who has landed everyone in trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Misguided' looks like an insult to the leader; it only supplies its own first letter. QU for queen is less common than Q or ER, but it is a dictionary abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A quagmire is a soggy bog and, figuratively, a hopeless mess — a pickle.

entries.clue: Victory by Germany’s a breeze (4)

blocks.note: D is Germany's international vehicle code (Deutschland)

annotation.surface: A German win in some contest turns out to have been easy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A breeze' reads as 'an easy task' in the surface; here it is literal moving air.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a breeze is simply moving air, a gentle wind, not the 'easy task' idiom the surface uses.

entries.clue: Heard Jagger drinks cocktails? (3-3)

indicators.note: what is heard is a sound, so the answer is spelt differently from what is said

blocks.note: Mick Jagger of the Rolling Stones; sups = drinks

annotation.surface: Rumour has it that Mick Jagger orders cocktails.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: cocktails are drinks mixed up, and mix-ups are muddles.
annotation.definitionFit: Cocktails are literally things mixed up, a playful stretch of mix-ups, meaning confusions.

entries.clue: Crepe tailored around female model is superb (7)

indicators.note: tailoring cuts and reshapes cloth, so the letters are refashioned
the rearranged letters go around the next piece

annotation.surface: A dress of crepe fabric, cut to fit a female model, looks superb.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all fashion: 'female model' reads as one person, but it splits into F and the Model T car.
annotation.definitionFit: Perfect and superb both mean excellent beyond improvement.

entries.clue: Was brought up having a tether on power tool (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up writes it bottom to top
in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

blocks.note: a chain can serve as a tether

annotation.surface: Someone raised on a farm, tied up, and a power tool is somehow involved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was brought up' reads as describing a childhood; it is the word WAS turned upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a motor-driven saw, a power tool.

entries.clue: Demonstrate heartily, loud as possible outside prison: outrage (10)

definitions.note: the definition is a noun but SCANDALOUS is an adjective: an outrage is something scandalous

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle
the letters could possibly form another word, so they are rearranged
the rearranged letters wrap around the prison

blocks.note: the letters of LOUD AS rearranged
the middle letter of the eleven in DEMONSTRATE

annotation.surface: A protester shouts as loudly as possible outside a jail about some outrage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loud as possible' reads as one phrase meaning at full volume; 'possible' is really the anagram signal. The S from the heart of 'demonstrate' closes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Something scandalous is an outrage: shocking and offensive.

entries.clue: Shot French girl during training session (6)

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it

annotation.surface: A French girl is hurt by a stray shot at a practice session.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a verb, something done to the girl; it is a noun, a piece of shot.
annotation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small ball of lead shot fired from a gun.

entries.clue: Firstly find uniform then give it repair for runaway (8)

indicators.note: take only the first letter
repairing puts pieces back in a new arrangement
'then' means next in sequence, so the anagram follows the F and U

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet
the letters of GIVE IT rearranged

annotation.surface: An instruction to track down a clothing item and mend it, apparently for someone on the run.
annotation.definitionFit: A fugitive is someone who has run away.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fixing a uniform; 'uniform' is only the letter U from the NATO phonetic alphabet.

entries.clue: Pawn taken by you earlier turned game (6)

indicators.note: the pawn goes with the next piece
turning a word round reverses it

blocks.note: to hock something is to pawn it
ye is the old form of you

annotation.surface: In a chess game, the opponent's pawn was captured by you earlier and the game turned.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is chess, so 'Pawn' reads as a piece; it is the verb, to pawn.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: hockey, played with sticks and a ball or puck, is one kind of game.

entries.clue: Old Impressionist’s not succeeded making a comeback (4)

indicators.note: 'not' cancels 'succeeded', whose standard abbreviation S is therefore struck out of the word
coming back means running backwards

blocks.note: Degas, the French Impressionist painter, minus S for succeeded

annotation.surface: An elderly Impressionist painter, once a failure, is enjoying a return to fame.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s in 'Impressionist’s' is 'is' in the surface but it helps signal the S of DEGAS; S for succeeded is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: aged describes a person who has lived many years, which is what old means.

entries.clue: International organisation has long year tackling China being hostile (10)

definitions.note: 'being hostile' is a participle phrase; UNFRIENDLY is the adjective, so read it as 'hostile'

indicators.note: the long year takes China on, following it

blocks.note: china = mate in rhyming slang (china plate), so a friend
l. is an abbreviation of long (as in longitude)

annotation.surface: The UN spends a long year dealing with a hostile China.
annotation.walkthrough: China is capitalised as the country in the surface; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a china is a friend.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an unfriendly attitude is a hostile one, lacking goodwill.

entries.clue: About to be contracted with American travelling show (6)

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, losing its end

blocks.note: CIRCA (about) with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: Someone is about to sign a contract with an American touring show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About to be contracted' reads as someone nearly signed up; 'contracted' means shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: A circus is a travelling show of acrobats, clowns and animals.

entries.clue: Angry person has course stopped by college following sign something’s wrong (10)

indicators.note: the course is plugged by the college, which sits inside it
the course comes after the sign

blocks.note: a cross marks an answer wrong

annotation.surface: A student is furious because their course has been halted by the college after some warning sign.
annotation.walkthrough: The C slips into PATH just before the H.
annotation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is a bad-tempered, grumpy person.

entries.clue: Injured person relaxed with telly, drained (8)

indicators.note: a drained word has had its contents emptied, leaving the outside letters

blocks.note: TELLY without its middle; telly is British for television

annotation.surface: Someone lounging in front of the TV ends up exhausted.
annotation.walkthrough: Casualty is also a long-running BBC hospital drama, so the telly in the surface is apt.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in news reports a casualty is anyone hurt or killed in an accident or war.

entries.clue: Regret right nipple’s last extra special piercing (7)

indicators.note: take the final letter only
the S goes through MORE, sitting inside it

annotation.surface: Someone regrets getting their right nipple pierced as a special extra.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' in the surface is body jewellery; here it puts S inside MORE, between R and E.
annotation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong done.

entries.clue: Religious practice in South Dakota is zealous (8)

indicators.note: the religious practice goes inside the state abbreviation

blocks.note: a rite is a religious practice

annotation.surface: A fervent religious practice is found in South Dakota.
annotation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword regular for religious; SD is the US postal code for South Dakota.
annotation.definitionFit: Spirited and zealous both mean full of energy and enthusiasm.

entries.clue: Passed out studies about women’s eggs (7)

indicators.note: turned about, the word runs backwards, and it also goes around the rest

blocks.note: dens are studies; DENS written backwards
an O looks like an egg

annotation.surface: Someone fainted while studying a paper about women's eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Studies' reads as research; it is rooms, dens. 'About' does double duty: reversing DENS and wrapping it around W and OO.
annotation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, so swooned means passed out.

entries.clue: Tea’s dull after real bubbly (4,4)

indicators.note: dull comes after the other piece
bubbling letters are churned up

annotation.surface: Tea seems dull after real champagne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Real bubbly' reads as genuine champagne; 'bubbly' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a black tea flavoured with bergamot.

entries.clue: Glide quickly has winter sportsperson securing race (7)

indicators.note: the skier holds the race safe inside

blocks.note: a skier does a winter sport
the TT is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

annotation.surface: A skier secures a win in a race by gliding quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Securing race' reads as winning it; it means holding TT inside.
annotation.definitionFit: To skitter is to move lightly and quickly across a surface.

entries.clue: Enjoys tickling component of game controller (8)

indicators.note: the answer is a component of the letters before it

annotation.surface: Someone enjoys fiddling with part of a video-game controller.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Component of' reads as part of the definition; it is the signal that the answer sits inside the words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A joystick is a lever used to control video games.

entries.clue: Love national sport having quiet surge (6)

annotation.surface: A nation's favourite sport enjoys a quiet boom in popularity.
annotation.definitionFit: An onrush is a surging rush forward.
annotation.walkthrough: Love is O because a zero score in tennis is called love; RU is rugby union, the sport.

entries.clue: Writer isn’t regularly in cheap restaurant (6)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals
those letters go in the writer

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, the everyday British word for one
the second and fourth letters of ISNT

annotation.surface: A writer is seldom seen in a cheap café.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' wants to be an author; in crosswords a writer is often a pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: bistros are small, modest French-style eating places, cheaper than a grand restaurant.

entries.clue: Awful bore traps Australian in pub (6)

indicators.note: awful letters are in a bad state, so rearranged
the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside

annotation.surface: A dreadful bore corners an Australian in a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British slang for a pub, so the surface setting is the answer itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional use: in British slang, somewhere you go to booze (drink) is a boozer, a pub.

entries.clue: Split most of money by family couple (5,2,3)

indicators.note: take all but the last letter
the pieces stand side by side

blocks.note: BREAD, slang for money, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A family couple divides up most of their money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a verb acting on the money; it is the definition, standing alone at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to break something in two is to split it into two parts.

entries.clue: Performance requires soprano with range (4)

indicators.note: the soprano comes together with the range

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of kitchen range, a big cast-iron stove

annotation.surface: A concert performance needs a soprano with a wide vocal range.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' is vocal range in the surface; it is a cooking stove. 'Performance' means a long, tiresome business, as in 'what a performance!'
annotation.definitionFit: A performance, in the informal sense of a drawn-out fuss, is a saga.

entries.clue: Bar put small work area inside (4)

indicators.note: the pieces are put side by side
the area goes inside the work

annotation.surface: A pub installs a small work area inside the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a pub counter in the surface; it is a bar of soap.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by form: soap is commonly sold as a solid bar, so 'bar' is a cryptic stand-in.

entries.clue: Take audible deep breath, essential to find the inner self (6)

indicators.note: what can be heard is a sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: to sigh is to take a deep breath

annotation.surface: Breathing deeply is presented as the essential route to finding your true self, as in meditation.
annotation.walkthrough: The meditation picture hides that 'audible' governs both parts: SIGH and KEY together sound like PSYCHE.
annotation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, the inner self.

entries.clue: Promoted first four in team by date applied (8)

indicators.note: keep only the first four letters
the letters are put to work in a new order

blocks.note: a team is an ELEVEN (football or cricket); its first four letters

annotation.surface: The first four players picked are promoted to the team on a set date.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Team' becomes a word, ELEVEN, the size of a football or cricket side, before it is trimmed.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an elevated employee has been raised to a higher rank, i.e. promoted.
